common_instruction: Answer as an engineer using the stated project and tool constraints; do not claim to have executed any checks.

cases.name: Optional config lookup
cases.prompt: A Go service uses spf13/viper v1.20. It searches default config paths and should work with environment variables alone when no file exists. Show error handling for ReadInConfig that distinguishes an optional missing search result from a malformed file.
cases.trap: An errors.As pointer-to-pointer target misses a value-typed ConfigFileNotFoundError and aborts startup.
expectations: Uses value-type ConfigFileNotFoundError with errors.As or an equivalent correct match.
Propagates actual read/parse errors and distinguishes an explicitly named missing path when necessary.
must_not: Does not swallow every ReadInConfig error or declare the file mandatory.

cases.name: Unmarshal env-only keys
cases.prompt: A viper service sets SetEnvPrefix("APP"), AutomaticEnv and a dot-to-underscore replacer. APP_DATABASE_HOST is present, but Unmarshal into Config.Database.Host yields empty when no file/default defines that key. Diagnose and propose a bounded fix.
cases.trap: AutomaticEnv Get works while Unmarshal enumerates registered AllKeys and drops env-only values.
expectations: Explains why direct Get and Unmarshal can differ for unregistered keys.

Makes the expected key available to Unmarshal via BindEnv or an appropriate default, or uses an explicitly mapped Get-based configuration path with equivalent values and precedence. Retains the configured prefix/replacer semantics; registration is not the only valid repair.
Proposes a real env-only regression check.
must_not: Does not claim AutomaticEnv automatically adds arbitrary environment keys to Unmarshal.

cases.name: required-file-does-not-fall-back
cases.prompt: A Go service using Viper accepts --config /etc/acme/prod.yaml. Its accepted startup contract says an explicitly selected file is required; defaults apply only when no path was selected. The loader calls SetConfigFile on that path, then ReadInConfig returns an error because the file is missing. A patch proposes swallowing it and continuing from environment values. Review that patch and state the error-handling rule.
cases.trap: Generalizes optional default-path search to every missing configuration file, silently ignoring the explicitly required input.
expectations: Rejects silently ignoring failure of the explicitly selected required path.
Separates optional search not-found behavior from required-file, parse and permission errors, without relying on one guessed concrete missing-file error type.
negative_expectations: Must not allow successful startup solely because environment values or defaults exist when the required file is unavailable.

cases.name: binding-after-parse-before-read
cases.prompt: In a Go command, pflag parsing completes before RunE. RunE first calls v.BindPFlag("port", cmd.Flags().Lookup("port")), checks the error, then calls v.GetInt("port"). There are no earlier Viper reads and no other command binds this key. A reviewer says the binding is necessarily too late because parsing already happened. Is that a bug? Explain the actual boundary.
cases.trap: Applies a before-Execute lifecycle rule even though Viper reads the bound flag lazily and all dependent reads happen after binding.
expectations: Recognizes this sequence can be correct: BindPFlag establishes the binding before the first GetInt that consumes it.
Explains that the relevant risks are an earlier dependent read or conflicting binding, neither of which is present in the supplied task.
negative_expectations: Must not require moving binding to init or before Execute solely because flags have already been parsed.
Must not introduce additional config sources or hot reload to solve this review question.
